class.name: SubtitleLabel
class.brief_description: A ready-made subtitle line that shows the segments of a [SubtitlePlayer] and follows the accessibility settings.

method.name: get_display_font_size
method.description: Returns the text size in use: [member font_size], scaled by [method AccessibilitySettingsServer.scale_subtitle_font_size] if [member follow_accessibility_settings] is enabled.

method.name: get_subtitle_text
method.description: Returns the BBCode of the lines to show now, the same text [method refresh] writes to [member RichTextLabel.text]. Empty while no line is shown, the subtitles are disabled or [member player] is not found.

method.name: refresh
method.description: Rebuilds the text from the active segments of [member player]. The label calls it on every segment change of the player, every change of the settings it follows ([AccessibilitySettingsServer], [member SubtitleServer.enabled], [member SubtitleServer.captions_enabled]), a locale change and when the player leaves the tree. Call it yourself after changing the dictionary returned by [member speaker_colors] in place.

members.member: If [code]true[/code], the label follows [AccessibilitySettingsServer]: it shows nothing while [member AccessibilitySettings.subtitles_enabled] is off, drops closed captions while [member AccessibilitySettings.captions_enabled] is off, and scales [member font_size] with [member AccessibilitySettings.subtitle_scale] and [member AccessibilitySettings.font_size_factor].
The base text size in pixels, before the accessibility scale. It applies to every font of the label (normal, bold, italics, mono) and is not a theme override.
The [SubtitlePlayer] whose segments are shown. It is resolved when the label is ready, so the player can come later in the scene, and again when the label re-enters the tree or the player leaves it.

The speaker of the sample line shown in the editor (see [member preview_text]). It uses [member show_speaker_names], the entry of [member speaker_colors] and the [DialogueSpeaker] of [member SubtitleServer.speakers] with this id, so the speaker styling can be tried out. The Inspector suggests the speaker ids. Only used in the editor.

The text of the sample line the label shows in the editor while no real line is visible, so it can be placed and styled (anchors, [member font_size], theme styles, background) without playing anything. It is never shown while the game runs. It is saved with the scene, but not translated.
If [code]true[/code], a dialog line with a [member SubtitleSegment.speaker] starts with the speaker's name and a colon, for example [code]Anna: Hello[/code]. Closed captions never show a speaker.

The text color of each speaker's lines, by [member SubtitleSegment.speaker]. A speaker without an entry uses [member DialogueSpeaker.color] of [member SubtitleServer.speakers]; white, its default, adds no color. Other lines and closed captions use the theme's text color ([code]default_color[/code]). Shown names come from [method SubtitleServer.get_display_speaker], so a known speaker shows its [member DialogueSpeaker.display_name].
